subject: PO metadata and invoice-release gating for enterprise commitment
messages:
From: Marta López <marta.lopez@healthsync.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO requirements / invoice cadence for Redwood sandbox pilot

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team likes the latency profile and the transparent unit economics. Procurement is asking us to confirm a couple of operational items before we proceed to a blanket PO:

- We need Redwood to accept a single master PO (one header) but ship invoices weekly against line-item consumption. Our AP system cannot accept multiple PO numbers per invoice; it needs the original PO ID on each invoice line.
- Standard net term for the account is net90. Will you accept net90 for the first 6 months while our contingent budget approvals finalize?
- We also require the PO header to include the internal BU code and an authorization token field for automated matching.

Attached is a sample of our PO export (HealthSync_PO_sample_2026-09-20.pdf). Can you confirm if Redwood can produce weekly invoices with the original PO ID and include the requested PO custom fields? Also any impact on pricing/discount eligibility if we move to net90 vs net45?

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement needs to close the paperwork to get legal moving.

Best,
Marta López
Director, Strategic Sourcing
HealthSync Medical

--
Attachment: HealthSync_PO_sample_2026-09-20.pdf (application/pdf, 54KB)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: Marta López <marta.lopez@healthsync.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements / invoice cadence for Redwood sandbox pilot

Hi Marta — thanks for the sample PO and the clear list. Quick answers up-front:

1) Weekly invoices with the original PO ID on each line: yes, we can emit weekly statements that include the PO header ID on every invoice line to satisfy AP matching. That will be generated from our billing pipeline.

2) PO custom fields (BU code, auth token): we can map two custom PO header fields into our invoice metadata if they appear consistently on the PO. If you can confirm the exact field names (BU_CODE and AUTH_TOKEN) we can add them to the invoice CSV/export and the PDF footer.

3) Net terms: Redwood standard hosted-tier discount bands are calibrated to net45 by default. We can accept net90 for onboarding on a short-term basis, but there are two trade-offs to be aware of:
   - Pricing/discounts: net90 will require a modest holdback on discount eligibility (typically a 2.5% reduction on committed-volume discount bands) because of receivables exposure.
   - Accounting ops: net90 invoices will still be generated weekly, but settlement dates will be 90 days from invoice date which will delay revenue recognition on our side.

Operational ask: if procurement needs net90 for the first 6 months, we can propose an interim amendment: accept net90 for months 1–6; if payments are timely we will reinstate the original discount bands (including any negotiated slab discounts) starting month 7. As a gesture we can also offer a one-time prepay credit equivalent to 1% of the first-month spend if HealthSync can pre-authorize a rolling payment tranche later.

Next steps: I’ve attached our latest PO template (Redwood_PO_Template_v3.pdf) showing the header fields we require for automated mapping. If you can provide the field names exactly as your ERP will emit them, we’ll confirm mapping and share an invoice sample.

Looping in Markus (Finance) and Ben (Sales) for term approval and discount alignment.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Redwood_PO_Template_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 22KB)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: PO requirements / invoice cadence for Redwood sandbox pilot

Markus / Ben — forwarding HealthSync’s PO asks. Key points: weekly invoices (with single PO ID on each line), need to accept net90 for first 6 months, and map two header fields (BU_CODE, AUTH_TOKEN). They sent a PO sample.

Proposal from my side: Accept net90 for months 1–6 subject to successful mapping validation and a small discount holdback: reduce committed-volume discount by 2.5% while on net90. Offer conditional reinstatement to full discount on month 7 if payments clear on schedule. Also offer a 1% first-month prepay credit if they agree to pre-authorize a rolling payment tranche (helps us with cash).

Questions for finance/legal: 1) any accounting or recognition red flags if we accept net90 for a pilot? 2) Contractual language — we should explicitly call this an "interim payment cadence amendment" to avoid changing the master SLA/commitment triggers. 3) Do we ok a clause that ties discount reinstatement to a simple payment-timeliness metric (no more than one late payment over the first 6 invoices)?

I’ve attached the PO sample and our template again. If you approve, I’ll update the amendment and send to Marta for signature.

Thanks,
Vanessa

--

Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and for outlining the trade-offs. Procurement and finance discussed internally and are prepared to accept the interim amendment you proposed with a couple of clarifications:

- HealthSync will provide the PO header with BU_CODE and AUTH_TOKEN fields exactly as named; we’ll confirm the export layout tomorrow.
- We are amenable to the 2.5% holdback while on net90, but request that the reinstatement metric be 0 late payments across the first 6 invoice cycles (we can automate remittance confirmations). If there is a single late payment we accept that reinstatement will be subject to review.
- We will sign an amendment that is explicitly timeboxed to 6 months and references the original SOW and SLA.

Please send the amendment and a sample weekly invoice PDF (with the PO header fields visible) and we’ll route to legal. Once legal signs, procurement will issue the master PO (single header).

Thanks again — Marta
